title: How Marc Lou made $6,000 in 48 hours with ShipFast: 4 launch lessons
summary: Marc recounts launching ShipFast, a Next.js boilerplate he built in a week to scratch his own itch, and earning more in 48 hours than in all of 2022. He draws four lessons: skip AI products, launch many startups before focusing, invest in basic design, and chase product-market fit where users pull out their credit cards.

principles.text: Build the thing you personally want; it's the surest way to make something people want.
principles.quote: So I built something I wanted—a code boilerplate to ship faster—and hoped people would need it too. I built it in a week, with no expectations, and launched it.

principles.text: Put a buy button on every project and build painkillers, not vitamins.
principles.quote: Always have a buy button on every project

principles.text: Avoid building AI products driven by FOMO; use AI to improve your workflow while building something else.
principles.quote: If you want to build with AI, build something else and see how AI could improve your workflow.

principles.text: Don't commit to a startup without traction. Launch many, see what sticks, then focus.
principles.quote: Don't try to make a startup work if there is no initial traction. Create a bunch of startups, see what sticks, and then focus.

principles.text: Design is your thumbnail and copy is your title. Good design is just padding, layout and typeface.
principles.quote: Your design is the YouTube thumbnail. Your copy is the video title. Visitors are caught by the design and stay for the copy.

principles.text: True product-market fit means users are pulled in; build something that makes buying a no-brainer.
principles.quote: Build something that makes users want to pull their credit cards like a no-brainer. Don't waste time on the rest.
